question.text: If $\alpha, \beta$ are the roots of the quadratic equation $x^{2}+p x+q=0,$ then the values of $\alpha^{3}+\beta^{3}$ and $\alpha^{4}+\alpha^{3} \beta^{2}+\beta^{4}$ are respectively

solution.text:
$\because$ Sum of roots, $\alpha+\beta=-p$ and $\alpha \beta=q$ $\therefore \quad\left(a^{3}+\beta^{3}\right)=(\alpha+\beta)^{3}-3 \alpha \beta(\alpha+\beta)$
$$
\begin{aligned}
=(-p)^{3}-3 q(-p) \\
=&-p^{3}+3 p q \\
&=\left(\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}\right)+(\alpha \beta)^{2} \\
&=\left(\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}\right)^{2}-(\alpha \beta)^{2} \\
&=\left[(\alpha+\beta)^{2}-2 \alpha \beta\right]^{2}-(\alpha \beta)^{2} \\
&=\left[(-p)^{2}-2 q\right]^{2}-3(q)^{2} \\
&=\left[p^{2}-2 q\right]^{2}-3 q^{2} \\
&=p^{4}-4 p^{2} q+4 q^{2}-q^{2} \\
&=p^{4}-4 p^{2} q+3 q^{2} \\
&=p^{4}-3 p^{2} q-p^{2} q+3 q^{2} \\
&=p^{2}\left(p^{2}-3 q\right)-q\left(p^{2}-3 q\right) \\
&=\left(p^{2}-q\right)\left(p^{2}-3 q\right)
\end{aligned}
$$
